summary: Pixel-for-pixel identical to the original on every rig size, seed and time window tested; the only divergence is that the port advances its colour phase exactly one rendered frame early (4 differing frames out of 160 in a full 8 s cycle).
observations: Structure (both sides, identical): a sparse index-based ruler. Lit pixels are index 0, every multiple of 10 (10, 20, 30, 40, 50 on the default 60 px strip) and the LAST pixel (59). All other pixels are exactly 0,0,0. Confirmed by --dump, not by eye.
Both endpoints stay white forever: pixel 0 and the last pixel are a constant 127,127,127 in every phase, on both sides. Only the interior decade markers change colour.

Colour cycle (both sides, identical): white 127,127,127 -> red 255,0,0 -> green 0,255,0 -> blue 0,0,255, each held for exactly 2.00 s, so an 8.00 s loop. Values are exact full-scale primaries and a 127 grey, no dimming, no fades, no interpolation between phases -- transitions are instantaneous single-frame steps.

Cadence verified over a 240 s / 2 fps survey (30 full loops): orig transitions at frames 4, 8, 12 ... 476 and port at 3, 7, 11 ... 479 -- gap set is exactly {4} on both sides (4 frames at 2 fps = 2.000 s). No drift accumulates: the port's lead is still exactly one frame at t=240 s, same as at t=2 s.

THE ONE DIVERGENCE: the port switches colour exactly one rendered frame before the original, at every boundary. Measured at 20 fps (orig switches at t=2.00, port at t=1.95), at 10 fps (2.00 vs 1.90) and at 40 fps (2.000 vs 1.975). Because the lead is always one FRAME and never a fixed number of seconds, this is an off-by-one in the phase/accumulator (the port evaluates its phase after advancing time, or one tick ahead), not a rate error.

Quantified: dumping all 160 consecutive frames of one full 8 s cycle at 20 fps, orig and port frames are byte-identical on 156 of 160; the 4 differing frames are t=1.95, 3.95, 5.95, 7.95 -- precisely the last frame of each 2 s colour segment. 2.5% of frames differ, and only at the instant of a step change.

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): the 2.00 s segment length holds at 10, 20 and 40 fps on both. The 10/20/40 diagnostic is corroborated by absolute transition TIMES from --dump, not by the motion stat.

Rig/geometry independence, identical on both sides: at --pixels 12 markers are {0, 10, 11}; at 37 {0, 10, 20, 30, 36}; at 120 {0,10,...,110, 119}; at 300 {0,10,...,290, 299}. The stride is a fixed 10 indices (not a fraction of the strip) and the final pixel is always added as an end marker -- port reproduces this exactly, including the degenerate 12 px case where markers 10 and 11 are adjacent.
Seed-independent: at --seed 1234 both sides render the same frames as at seed 1 (no randomness in this pattern).

Steady state is healthy on both sides: at --skip 120 (t=120-130 s) frames are byte-identical between orig and port at all ten sampled seconds, and the cycle is still running on schedule. brightnessTrend reads 'decaying' on both in the 6 s baseline, which is a window artefact (white 15 -> red 4 mean-B) and not a decay -- mean brightness is flat at 12-13 over 240 s on both sides.

motion stat is a poor lens here (only ~11% of pixels lit and static between transitions): baseline zeroMotionFrames 118/120 on orig and 117/120 on port with motion.max 14. motionLit.max is 121.4 on both, confirming the transitions are full-amplitude on the lit set. The 1-frame port lead is exactly why the port posts one fewer zero-motion frame.

Control surface: BOTH sides expose zero controls (meta.json sides.orig.controls == [] and sides.port.controls == []), and --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for each. No control-surface mismatch.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), so sensors are irrelevant to this pattern.
No compile or runtime errors on either side in any of the ~18 runs.
feedback: Only one thing to fix, and it is cosmetic: the port's colour phase runs exactly one rendered frame ahead of the original. Every segment boundary lands one frame early -- orig turns red at t=2.00 s, port at t=1.95 s (20 fps), t=1.90 s (10 fps), t=1.975 s (40 fps). The lead scales with the frame interval, so the port is advancing its time accumulator before evaluating the phase (or seeding it at one tick rather than zero) where the original evaluates first, then advances. Shifting the phase evaluation by one tick (or initialising the accumulator to 0 instead of dt) makes the two sides byte-identical.

Do NOT change the segment duration or the cycle length while fixing the above: 2.000 s per colour / 8.000 s per loop is already exact on both sides and holds over 30 consecutive loops with zero drift. The bug is a phase offset, not a rate error.

Everything else is already correct and should be left alone: marker set {0, every 10th index, last index}, constant white 127,127,127 endpoints, exact primaries 255,0,0 / 0,255,0 / 0,0,255, grey 127,127,127, instantaneous transitions with no fade, index-based stride that does not scale with pixel count, and correct behaviour at tiny (12 px) and large (300 px) rigs.
No dial work needed: the original genuinely exposes no controls and the port correctly exposes none either.
